2: 
3: Use this procedure for each literature E whose original text is missing. Both
4: the NL0 author and global Audit A reviewer follow it. Reuse an already supplied,
5: hash-bound primary document instead of downloading it again. The invoking agent
6: may retrieve sources before dispatch, but every supplied document must be an
7: explicit input; never insert files into an active run's frozen inputs.
8: 
9: ## 1. Identify the requested work and edition
10: 
11: Read the actual citation and its use in the supplied proof. Record author,
12: title, known arXiv ID/version or DOI, source kind, and expected theorem/lemma,
13: page or equation. Search terms must come from that material. Do not invent an
14: identifier or accept a nearby search hit. A shared title does not establish
15: that two editions have the same statements or numbering.
16: 
17: ## 2. Try arXiv first
18: 
19: Call `search_external_sources(query=title_and_authors, engine="arxiv")`. If an
20: arXiv ID is already given, use that exact ID, including its version suffix.
21: Read the matching abstract/version record, then use `read_external_source` on
22: the actual PDF link. The search tool exposes PDF locators from arXiv abstract
23: links; those locators are not a substitute for downloading the PDF.
24: 
25: Check identity, version, page count and the complete relevant result. Follow
26: its definitions and standing hypotheses. If only another version is available,
27: compare the relevant statements and their conventions, or continue searching
28: for the cited edition. Never copy a page number from a different version.
29: Stop retrieval when an adequate original has actually been obtained.
30: 
31: ## 3. Search Google for the complete text
32: 
33: If the needed original is still missing, call
34: `search_external_sources(query=title_and_authors, engine="google")`. Open
35: plausible author, institution, repository or publisher links and download the
36: full document with `read_external_source`. A title-only result, catalog,
37: abstract, search snippet or AI overview does not verify an external theorem.
38: 
39: For `BROWSER_REQUIRED` or a verification page, retry the same search/read with
40: `browser=true`. The controller can use an installed, isolated local Chrome
41: through the fixed optional helper. It performs real navigation and rendered
42: readback, preserves screenshots and uses no personal browser profile. This
43: also works for CLI stages without a desktop tab-control tool. Missing browser
44: dependencies, unresolved challenges and browser failures are explicit records;
45: they do not stop the mathematical workflow by themselves.
46: 
47: An invoking agent with an actual built-in-browser control tool may instead use
48: that frontend and stage the downloaded original before dispatch. Opening or
49: queuing a tab alone is never readback evidence. Do not claim that a headless
50: Chrome session is the user's visible in-app tab.
51: 
52: ## 4. Find and confirm a DOI, then try Sci-Hub
53: 
54: When full text remains missing, search Google again using the exact title,
55: authors and `DOI`. Inspect `doi_candidates` and the linked publisher or DOI
56: metadata; confirm title, author and edition. These strings are only candidate
57: identifiers. Reuse a DOI already established by the supplied bibliography or
58: matching primary metadata; a blocked Google page need not prevent that lookup.
59: Do not guess a DOI or request an unrelated article just to make retrieval pass.
60: 
61: Call `search_external_sources(query=confirmed_doi, engine="scihub", browser=true)`.
62: The controller navigates to `https://sci-hub.box/<DOI>`. Ordinary site controls,
63: including its own ALTCHA verification button when present, may complete normal
64: access. Follow the returned PDF/object link through `read_external_source`.
65: Record any redirect, including a different mirror's final hostname, rather
66: than claiming the bytes came from the initial host. Do not fabricate challenge
67: tokens, import personal cookies, silently purchase access or change system
68: proxy settings. If a challenge cannot be completed normally, retain the failure
69: and move to the disclosed conditional route.
70: 
71: ## 5. Establish source fidelity after retrieval
72: 
73: Retain the actual URL, final URL, retrieval timestamp, document/text hashes and
74: access receipt. A fetched PDF is a readable source candidate, not an automatic
75: truth or theorem-fidelity judgment. Apply [external-theorem review](external-theorems.md):
76: confirm author/title/version, locate the result, read the full statement and
77: governing definitions, check corrections/version history where available, and
78: map every hypothesis, conclusion and constant dependency to E. Each application
79: still needs its own verified substitutions and premise checks. A source that
80: states a different theorem is a mismatch, not an inaccessible-text deferral.
81: 
82: For a changed edition, retain both document hashes and a locator/statement map.
83: Do not silently substitute the journal version for a cited preprint. Any
84: substantive normalization bridge belongs in an internal proved node.
85: 
86: ## 6. Record unavailable verification and continue
87: 
88: After actual unsuccessful retrieval, follow [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md).
89: Supply `defer_primary_source` with the E ID, a complete exact quotation already
90: present in a declared secondary input, its input ID and own failed
91: `access_records` paths. An unavailable original does not justify inventing a
92: statement from memory or treating a known contradiction as an assumption.
93: If the statement itself is missing or incomplete, identify that missing content
94: instead of pretending the source-only route closes the proof.
95: 
96: Retain `UNVERIFIED_PRIMARY`, `warn.json` and `warn.md`. Continue all other
97: mathematical, Lean, assembly and audit work normally. The final result remains
98: `WORKFLOW-CONDITIONAL` (or the corresponding stage's conditional status) until
99: the actual source and affected review are completed. Display each warning to
100: the user when it arises and in the final answer. A compile pass does not remove
101: source uncertainty. Do not repeat indefinitely an unchanged blocked query;
102: preserve its failure and advance to the next route.
103: 
104: ## Optional local browser setup
105: 
106: No browser package is installed automatically. `nl0/scripts/source_browser.py`
107: looks for Node on PATH or the bundled Codex runtime, its bundled Playwright,
108: and an installed Chrome/Chromium. Other installations can set:
109: 
110: ```sh
111: export YUI_SOURCE_BROWSER_NODE="/absolute/path/to/node"
112: export YUI_SOURCE_BROWSER_MODULE="/absolute/path/to/playwright/index.mjs"
113: export YUI_SOURCE_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE="/absolute/path/to/chrome"
114: ```
115: 
116: These select existing host tools, not model-generated commands or scripts. An
117: invalid explicit override is reported without silently choosing another tool.
118: The trusted driver is included in frozen runtime hashes. Each call owns its
119: temporary Chrome profile and process group; cancellation and a transport wait
120: timeout close those processes. The wait timeout is a browser operation limit,
121: not a case/proof budget. Source readback keeps the existing 32 MiB file limit.
122: An unavailable browser leaves ordinary HTTPS and conditional continuation usable."}

3: [Audit A's shared requirements](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)

5: guide. Follow the table IDs, not an independently maintained approximation of
6: what the auditor might want. The clean carrier supplies that exact frozen
7: section to both roles. [The schema](nl0-format.md) describes serialization;
8: [the author template](../templates/authoring.md) gives tool shapes and examples.
9: The elementary permissions come from the same controller-owned foundation.
10: Use ordinary rigorous mathematical granularity. Explicitly register important
11: tools; eligible tiny background uses can be checked and recorded by Audit A
12: under [mathematical-background admission](background-notes.md). Do not pre-emptively
13: rebuild elementary theories or treat an omitted basic M ID as a substantive gap.
14: 
15: ## 1. Understand and freeze the supplied work
16: 
17: Read the original target and entire supplied proof. Identify its phases and
18: potential gaps, without adopting an alternative research route. Extract the
19: original H, parameters and definition pairs into spec.json. Preserve their
20: source locations. This supplies the `target` check; naming a condition inside
21: a parameter type does not satisfy its H inventory. Inspect material endpoint,
22: zero-object and ambient-dimension cases before building the graph.
23: Each H must itself state the complete given condition; phrases such as
24: "as specified in the target" do not supply that condition to a packet reader.
25: When an original GIVEN passage is already adequate, select its exact frozen
26: lines for `spec.hypotheses[i].statement`, using the same literal binding as D
27: definitions and S text. Preserve its origin and distinguish original givens
28: from desired conclusions and claims established later in the proof. Copying
29: does not turn those latter claims into hypotheses or certify fidelity.
30: 
31: Inventory each object's construction guards before exporting it with a type.
32: If a guard is a result of this work, establish it in an earlier N producer
33: before using the guarded D; do not promise that a later argument will make the
34: current declaration well-defined. Alternatively specify an actually total
35: construction and prove its intended property separately. Do not add a missing
36: guard as an original H. This is graph organization along the given proof,
37: not permission to change that proof or its hypotheses.
38: When the original already gives a complete adequate definition, use the
39: explicit frozen-input line binding for D.definition if helpful. This preserves
40: the selected text and its provenance without granting a property. Rewriting
41: notation still requires a complete faithful definition and its declarations.

160: derive it locally, export a proved N, or supply an exactly verified source.

10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound mathematically reviewed background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements

22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.

25: local mathematical facts and record precise statements, available conditions

27: query is required for ordinary background. These notes add neither H nor a
28: core proof route. Mathematical uncertainty still blocks. See
29: [background notes](background-notes.md).

32: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
33: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and

35: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule

37: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed

42: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
43: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
44: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
45: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
46: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.

48: ## Object closure
49: 
50: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
51: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
52:

55:    cover only core typed syntax, not a dictionary of subject-specific objects.

61: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact

73: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy

2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.

8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning."}

385: `ensure_ascii=False`, `separators=(",", ":")`) excluding `packet_sha256`.

389: ## Mechanical boundaries
390: 
391: The checker validates declared objects, the frozen contract, graph closure,
392: notation-name metadata, citation parity, local-assumption accounting, guarded
393: definition availability, and hash-bound audit coverage. It verifies source
394: checkout/file hashes, not the truth of a source restatement. The printed
395: signature must be obtained from a successful pinned Lean probe and compared by
396: the auditor; an arbitrary string called `signature` is not verification.

399: that two spellings have the same mathematical meaning, that a hidden theorem
400: was not used, that a local witness did not escape the prose, or that an argument
401: is valid. Those are explicit Audit A obligations. Neither a JSON PASS nor a
402: fabricated complete audit receipt is a mathematical certificate.
403: Numbered-reference diagnostics reject common opaque references, not every
404: possible paraphrase or hidden import. Behavioral tests must actually ask an
405: auditor to review unseen controls; manually prefilled FAIL records only test
406: receipt rejection and must be reported as such.

412: actual justification; native lookup is not required. A new supplemented replay

414: retain their complete bound library evidence; mathematical/elementary notes

416: variant consumers must reject unsupported receipts instead of dropping fields.

2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning."}

24: 
25: ### Scope and mathematical boundary
26: 
27: Global review owns target/H fidelity, definitions, source statements and graph
28: consistency. Each local reviewer owns the conditional implication at its R
29: node. Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary: these statements are conditional premises.
30: The local reviewer does not re-prove an input N or re-audit its source paper;
31: the graph and that producer's review establish those separate obligations.
32: Conversely, an input N exports only its full statement, not unexported facts
33: from the producer's body. The fifth local criterion, packet_replay, assesses
34: sufficiency under this exact boundary. The controller records execution
35: identity and exposure independently of the mathematical judgment.
36: 
37: Review correctness rather than the number of displayed lines. Ordinary valid
38: textbook compression is allowed. Material missing hypotheses, witnesses,
39: constructions, scope discharges or core arguments are not implementation gaps.
40: Return them for located author repair and fresh review. No theorem needs to be re-proved
41: when its legitimate mathematical source and actual application suffice.
42: 
43: The domain-neutral elementary-language-4 profile retains equality, supplied
44: definitions, finite arithmetic/order reasoning and finite sums. It is syntax
45: and elementary calculation policy, not a subject vocabulary or theorem list.
46: Objects from any field use problem parameters, D definitions or scoped locals.
47: Neither an author-written calculation list nor a familiar symbol adds a theorem.
48: 
49: ### Mathematical background: mathematical-background-v2-1
50: 
51: A reviewer may positively assess a routine, local mathematical fact without
52: first finding its Mathlib declaration. Record its precise mathematical
53: statement, actual argument location, available condition grounds and a short
54: mathematical justification in a background note. Use kind mathematical for an
55: ordinary background result and elementary for a useful elementary completion.
56: This is an actual mathematical judgment, not a future TODO or a claim of
57: native verification. Do not record every algebraic operation.
58: 
59: Eligibility requires a correct standard local step with all premises already
60: available, no new H and no substantial new core proof or changed route.
61: Important external tools remain explicit E inputs; a missing project result
62: or uncertain source cannot be waived as background. If an explicitly supplied
63: native mathlib note is retained, its full bound evidence is still validated.
64: No field-specific whitelist determines eligibility.
65: 
66: The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus its hash-bound mathematical
67: review supplement. It is a natural-language audit under the mathematical-background policy, not a
68: detailed-NL0 format-3 native-background receipt. At nl02lean, workers must discharge all necessary
69: facts by actual Lean proofs or checked library use; a note never becomes an
70: unproved H, axiom or extra external assumption. The exact implementation may
71: differ while preserving the mathematical meaning.
72: 
73: ### Actual review and result qualification
74: 
75: Independent reviewers assess the actual content; schema validation does not
76: prove mathematics. An unexamined item remains unread/read. A mathematical
77: uncertainty is assessed UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Missing or conflicting assessments
78: block acceptance. Ordinary source-access deferral follows the conditional-source
79: policy and must appear in final warnings; it cannot yield unqualified PASS.
80: 
81: Use short located reasons for straightforward PASS items and enough detail to
82: make a defect or uncertainty actionable. Avoid duplicate explanations across
83: criteria. A concise report still covers every required mathematical check.
84: Do not read author self-check notes, old verdicts, other R proof bodies, other
85: case results or personal proof skills to manufacture independent approval.

89: 
90: 1. Freeze the original problem, spec and NL0. A separate fresh global reviewer
91:    reads the exhaustive global-overview.json, relevant canonical content and
92:    source evidence. Review each D and selected E/M; the overview is data, not
93:    an assessment. Do not infer absence from a partial page.
94: 2. Complete global source/graph review before dispatching local R reviews.
95:    Up to the explicitly confirmed N independent R reviewers work concurrently.
96:    Each receives only its own packet and mathematical-NL0 rules. Review full arguments,
97:    actual applications and definitions; input N statements are conditional.
98: 3. Prefer one complete artifact with an explicit coverage map. Use
99:    record_review_item and read_review_progress only for useful checkpoints.
100:    record_background_note is optional; a complete artifact may include its
101:    actual notes directly. Batch reading several declared fragments is available.
102: 4. Each local report has inference, packet_sha256, verdict, notes, checks,
103:    findings and optional background_notes. The checks map contains exactly
104:    statement_closure, dependency_closure, argument, applicability, packet_replay.
105:    Each row has verdict, notes and resolving packet locations. E applications
106:    additionally retain actual binding, per-hypothesis, conclusion and bridge
107:    assessments; this is mathematical applicability, not a Lean API inventory.
108: 5. Global reports have target_review, definition_reviews, source_reviews,
109:    structure_review and findings. Each E adds citation_checks for

112:    leaves blocked checks UNVERIFIED while remaining assessment continues.

114:    quotation from that location. Preserve the defect and untouched coverage.
115:    Return located mathematical repairs to the author; review changed scopes
116:    independently. Do not resample a mathematical rejection or silently erase it.
117: 7. The collector checks complete coverage, consistency, exact bytes and actual
118:    independent execution before producing the audit-format-4 receipt.
119:    Old detailed-NL0 format-3 receipts are not silently upgraded. Inherited format-4 judgments retain
120:    their original source/rule hashes, exposure and costs.
121: 
122: ## Sources, scopes and final handoff
123: 
124: Use [external theorem review](external-theorems.md) and
125: [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md) for source identity, exact
126: statements and warnings. Reuse adequate original text; several theorem uses
127: may share one staged readback. Each application still discharges its own
128: premises. No successful download or guessed Mathlib availability is approval.
129: 
130: Use [logical rules](logical-rules.md) for local scopes and
131: [background notes](background-notes.md) for the mathematical supplement.

133: An inaccessible E original permits only a source-qualified result. Translation

9: reviews a complete natural-language proof and necessary mathematical detail.

15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |

28: consistency. Each local reviewer owns the conditional implication at its R
29: node. Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary: these statements are conditional premises.

31: the graph and that producer's review establish those separate obligations.
32: Conversely, an input N exports only its full statement, not unexported facts
33: from the producer's body. The fifth local criterion, packet_replay, assesses
34: sufficiency under this exact boundary. The controller records execution
35: identity and exposure independently of the mathematical judgment.

38: textbook compression is allowed. Material missing hypotheses, witnesses,
39: constructions, scope discharges or core arguments are not implementation gaps.

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change."}

spec.full_target:
# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.

argument.text: Fix m, A and s as declared. Apply M001 to the Euclidean metric space R^m, its Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale, the formula's covers are exactly the covers in D002: a countable family can be enumerated by natural numbers, padding with empty sets if finite, and conversely a sequence is countable. All nonempty sets allowed at such a scale are bounded, so their extended diameters equal their ordinary finite Euclidean diameters. Empty members have cost zero in both definitions; since s>0, nonempty singletons also have zero cost. Thus the inner infimum is exactly the supplied scale content. The extra scale infinity in M001 adds nothing to the supremum: its admissible covers include all covers at scale 1, so its infimum is at most the scale-1 content. The finite positive extended scales are precisely the positive real scales. Taking their supremum proves F001: H^s(A)=μH[s](A). No dimensional normalization constant is introduced.

Discharge L1 and record F000.

argument.text: For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. Such covers exist, for example by the finite-ball-cover assertion in N002. This is the existence statement F001, before choosing W.

produces.statement: There exists a sequence W of subsets of R^n covering E, with diam(W_i)≤r for all i and sum_i diam(W_i)^q<epsilon/2.

argument.text: Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

produces.statement: The family (U_i)_(i∈K) covers E, 0<r_i≤r≤1 for i∈K, r_i=diam(U_i), and sum_(i∈K)r_i^q<epsilon.

argument.text:
For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

produces.statement: H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.

argument.text: For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. N001, with ambient dimension n+1 and positive exponent q+1, gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). Discharge L3 and L2. This proves F004.

produces.statement: If n≥1, dim_H(F)≤D+1.

argument.text: A natural dimension n is either zero or at least one. F000 and F004 thus give dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. By N002 the right hand side is finite, proving the finiteness clause as well.

locals.type: sequence of subsets of Euclidean R^(n+1)
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary sequence V, temporarily a delta-cover of F.

locals.type: sequence of finite nonnegative real numbers
locals.declaration: Set rho_i=diam(V_i); empty members have rho_i=0.
Set A_i(i)={x∈R^n: there exists t∈R with (x,t)∈V_i}, the horizontal coordinate projection.
Set B_i(i)={t∈R: there exists x∈R^n with (x,t)∈V_i}, the vertical coordinate projection.
Set c equal to the finite real value of H^s_delta(E); N002 proves its finiteness for the positive s and delta.

locals.type: sequence of open subsets of R, each empty or an open bounded interval
locals.declaration: If V_i is nonempty set J_i=(inf(B_i)-eta_i/2,sup(B_i)+eta_i/2); if V_i is empty set J_i=empty.
For all natural i define f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t), with extended nonnegative values. Openness of J_i proves the measurability asserted here in S003.

locals.type: measure on the Borel real line
locals.declaration: Set μ=λ|I, Lebesgue measure restricted to I.

argument.text: Fix s>0, delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L1: V covers F and diam(V_i)≤delta for all i. Empty members may be discarded; equivalently retain them with all ensuing projections and intervals empty and costs zero. Define rho,A_i,B_i and c as declared. Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz for the Euclidean metric in D006: each squared coordinate distance is bounded by the sum of the squared horizontal and vertical distances. Hence diam(A_i),diam(B_i)≤rho_i≤delta. In particular a nonempty B_i is a nonempty bounded subset of R. N002 applies to the positive s,delta and gives c<infinity.

produces.statement: V covers F, rho_i≤delta, diam(A_i)≤rho_i, diam(B_i)≤rho_i, and c=H^s_delta(E)<infinity; nonempty B_i are bounded.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary epsilon>0 and set eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0. Define J as declared. For a nonempty B_i, its supremum minus its infimum equals its diameter and is at most rho_i by F001. Thus B_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i. The empty-member convention makes both assertions true for empty V_i as well. The J_i are open measurable sets and enclose the possibly nonmeasurable projections. This construction needs no measurability of V_i,A_i or B_i.

produces.statement: For every i, B_i⊆J_i, J_i is open and measurable, and |J_i∩I|≤|J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i.

argument.text: Define the nonnegative functions f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t). They are measurable because each J_i is open and each coefficient is a fixed finite nonnegative real. Under L2: t∈I, for every x∈E the point (x,t) lies in F, so some V_i contains it. Then x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Thus the family of A_i with t∈J_i is a delta-cover of E, and the defining infimum and diam(A_i)≤rho_i give c≤sum_i rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The point x here is universally bound in this coverage argument, and i is its existential cover index. Discharge L2 into the assertion for every t∈I. Record F003.

produces.statement: Each f_i is nonnegative and Borel measurable; for every u∈I, c≤sum_i f_i(u).

argument.text:
Set μ=λ|I. It is a measure on the Borel real line with μ(R)=λ(I)=1. Apply M006 with α=R, its Borel structure, index type β=N, this measure μ and the functions f of F003. Borel measurability implies μ-almost-everywhere measurability for each summand. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral and the integral of a constant on a set of measure one give
c≤∫_I sum_i f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i ∫_I f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i rho_i^s |J_i∩I|
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i rho_i^s
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.
Here the middle equality is the integral of a measurable indicator times its nonnegative coefficient. The first inequality inside the sum uses F002 and distributivity of nonnegative sums. Finally eta_i rho_i^s=epsilon*2^(-i-1)*rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)≤epsilon*2^(-i-1), whose sum is epsilon. All sums and integrals are nonnegative and may be infinite; c is finite by F001. This is F004.

produces.statement: c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.

argument.text: If sum_i rho_i^(s+1)=infinity, c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1) holds immediately. Otherwise F004 holds for every epsilon>0 with c and V fixed, so letting epsilon decrease to zero gives the same inequality c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1). The cover V was arbitrary under L1. Take the infimum over all its possible delta-covers of F and discharge L1, obtaining H^s_delta(E)≤H^(s+1)_delta(F). Since s>0 and delta>0 were arbitrary, this is precisely N005.

applications.bindings: Set α=R, m=borel(R), μ=λ restricted to I, β=N, and f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t).
hypothesis_checks: D008 gives Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line; restriction to the Borel interval I is a measure on that same measurable space, as defined at S004.
The index type is N, which is countable.
F003, established in S003 from openness of J_i and constant nonnegative coefficients, proves Borel measurability of every f_i, hence almost-everywhere measurability for the restricted measure.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary positive lower bound T.

argument.text: Temporarily assume L1: D>0 and L2: 0<s<D for arbitrary real s. N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. By its definition as the supremum of scale contents, for every T>0 there exists delta>0 with H^s_delta(E)>T. Moreover these contents are nondecreasing as scale decreases, because a cover admissible at a smaller scale is admissible at any larger one. Thus such lower bounds also hold at arbitrarily small scales. N005 applies at each such delta and gives H^(s+1)_delta(F)≥H^s_delta(E)>T. Its supremum is therefore infinite: H^(s+1)(F)=infinity. Since s+1>0, N001 gives dim_H(F)≥s+1. Record F001.

produces.statement: dim_H(F)≥s+1.

argument.text: By N002, D is a finite real number; under L1 it is positive. F001 holds for every s with 0<s<D. Such s can increase to D, so their s+1 have supremum D+1 and dim_H(F)≥D+1. Equivalently any number below D+1 is below some s+1 with 0<s<D. Discharge L2 in this universal limiting argument, and then discharge L1 to obtain the full conditional statement N006.

locals.type: sequence of subsets of Euclidean R^(n+1)
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary sequence V, temporarily a delta-cover of F.

argument.text: Temporarily assume L1: D=0. By H002 choose x_0∈E and define f(t)=(x_0,t). The Euclidean metric formula in D006 gives dist(f(t),f(u))=|t-u| for all real t,u, including n=0. Thus f restricts to an isometric embedding of I into F.

produces.statement: The restriction of f to I is an isometric embedding and f(I)⊆F.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary s under L2: 0<s<1. For any delta>0 and arbitrary V under L3: V is a delta-cover of F, define W as declared. F001 shows W covers I, and isometry gives diam(W_i)≤diam(V_i)≤delta. Hence H^s_delta(I)≤sum_i diam(V_i)^s. Take the infimum over V, discharge L3, and then take the supremum over positive delta to get H^s(I)≤H^s(F). This proves the particular dimension-monotonicity implication used here directly from covers. N003 gives H^s(I)=infinity, so H^s(F)=infinity. N001 applied to F and exponent s yields dim_H(F)≥s.

produces.statement: dim_H(F)≥s.

argument.text: Since F002 holds for every s with 0<s<1, letting s increase to 1 gives dim_H(F)≥1. Discharge L2. Under L1, 1=D+1, so this proves the asserted bound. Discharge L1 to obtain N007. The argument used only the isometric embedding from a point of E, and applies unchanged to the singleton ambient space R^0.

N002 gives finite D≥0. Thus either D>0 or D=0. In the positive case N006 gives dim_H(F)≥D+1; in the zero case N007 gives the identical bound, including n=0. N004 supplies dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. Antisymmetry gives dim_H(F)=D+1. Substituting F=E×[0,1] and D=dim_H(E), with the Euclidean identification of D006, proves the complete target P.

spec.full_target:
# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
spec.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, with R^n×R identified with Euclidean R^(n+1), including n=0.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary positive real exponent s.

argument.text: Fix m, A and s as declared. Apply M001 to the Euclidean metric space R^m, its Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale, the formula's covers are exactly the covers in D002: a countable family can be enumerated by natural numbers, padding with empty sets if finite, and conversely a sequence is countable. All nonempty sets allowed at such a scale are bounded, so their extended diameters equal their ordinary finite Euclidean diameters. Empty members have cost zero in both definitions; since s>0, nonempty singletons also have zero cost. Thus the inner infimum is exactly the supplied scale content. The extra scale infinity in M001 adds nothing to the supremum: its admissible covers include all covers at scale 1, so its infimum is at most the scale-1 content. The finite positive extended scales are precisely the positive real scales. Taking their supremum proves F001: H^s(A)=μH[s](A). No dimensional normalization constant is introduced.

produces.statement: H^s(A)=μH[s](A).

argument.text: Use F001 to transport the four critical-exponent facts. Under L1: 0<s<dim_H(A), M002 with nonnegative exponent a=s gives μH[s](A)=infinity, hence H^s(A)=infinity; discharge L1. Under L2: dim_H(A)<s, M003 gives μH[s](A)=0, hence H^s(A)=0; discharge L2. Under L3: H^s(A)=0, F001 makes μH[s](A)=0≠infinity, and M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L3. Under L4: H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L4. These are the complete conditional assertions F002.

produces.statement: If 0<s<dim_H(A), H^s(A)=infinity; if dim_H(A)<s, H^s(A)=0; if H^s(A)=0, dim_H(A)≤s; if H^s(A)=infinity, dim_H(A)≥s.

argument.text: The dimension in D004 is a supremum in the nonnegative extended reals, so it is nonnegative, including for the empty set. The arbitrary choices of m,A,s and F001-F002 prove every clause of N001.

locals.declaration: Choose b>0 with E⊆[-b,b]^n as supplied by F001.
Let h be an arbitrary mesh size, temporarily 0<h≤1.

argument.text: By H003, E is compact, hence bounded in its Euclidean metric. A bounded subset of R^n is contained in a coordinate box [-b,b]^n for some b>0: each coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance, and increasing a bound if necessary makes it positive. This also holds in R^0. Record F001. H001 specifies the nonnegative ambient dimension; N001 gives D≥0.

produces.statement: There exists a positive real b with E⊆[-b,b]^n.

argument.text: Choose b from F001 and define C as declared. Under L1: n>0, fix arbitrary a and h under L2: a>n and L3: 0<h≤1. Divide each coordinate interval [-b,b] into ceil(2b/h) intervals of side at most h. Their number is at most (2b+1)/h in each coordinate, hence the resulting at most C h^(-n) closed cubes cover E. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h. Therefore their total a-cost is at most C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a=C n^(a/2)h^(a-n). Since a-n>0, this tends to zero as h decreases to zero, and their diameters also tend to zero. In particular, at each fixed target scale arbitrarily small h provides admissible covers with costs tending to zero, so H^a(E)=0. Discharge L3 after using the arbitrary mesh sizes. N001 with A=E, exponent a gives D≤a. Since a>n was arbitrary, D≤n (if D>n, choose a strictly between n and D). Discharge L2 and L1. This proves F002.

produces.statement: If n>0, then D≤n.

argument.text: Under L4: n=0, Euclidean R^0 consists of its single empty-coordinate point. H002 implies E=R^0. A cover by that singleton has diameter and s-cost zero for every positive exponent s. Thus H^s(E)=0 for all s>0, and N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, whence D=0 using D≥0. Discharge L4. By H001 the alternatives n=0 and n>0 exhaust the ambient dimensions. F002 and this branch give 0≤D≤n, so D is finite, with the stated singleton conclusion when n=0.

produces.statement: 0≤D≤n, D is finite, and n=0 implies E=R^0 and D=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary positive s and delta. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at the points of E form an open cover. By H003 there is a finite subcover, and each such ball has diameter at most delta. Its finite number of members and finite diameters give a finite total s-cost. The defining infimum therefore gives H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this proves N002.

locals.declaration: Let N range over the positive integers.

locals.type: sequence of finite nonnegative real numbers
sequence of open subsets of R, each empty or an open bounded interval
locals.declaration: For nonempty V_i set J_i=(inf(V_i)-epsilon*2^(-i-2),sup(V_i)+epsilon*2^(-i-2)); set J_i=empty for empty V_i.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary a under L1: a>1. For each positive integer N, divide I into N closed intervals of length 1/N. They have total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a), which tends to zero as N tends to infinity, while their maximum diameter tends to zero. Thus at every positive target scale the defining infimum is zero, and H^a(I)=0. N001 applied with ambient dimension 1 gives dim_H(I)≤a; taking a down to 1 gives dim_H(I)≤1. Discharge L1 and record F001, including the universally quantified zero-measure assertion.

produces.statement: dim_H(I)≤1, and for every real u>1, H^u(I)=0.

argument.text: Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L2: V is a delta-cover of I. Define rho as declared; each rho_i≤delta is finite. Fix epsilon>0 and define J as declared. A nonempty V_i is bounded, so its real supremum and infimum exist and sup(V_i)-inf(V_i)=rho_i. Therefore V_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1), also when V_i is empty. The open sets J_i cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure and |I|=1 give 1≤sum_i |J_i|≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon, using sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-1)=1. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the required inequality is immediate; if finite, letting the arbitrary epsilon decrease to zero yields F002: sum_i rho_i≥1. All sets measured here are open intervals or I, so no measurability of V_i is assumed.

produces.statement: sum_i rho_i≥1.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary s under L3: 0<s<1. For each i with rho_i>0, rho_i≤delta and s-1<0 give rho_i^s=rho_i*rho_i^(s-1)≥delta^(s-1)*rho_i. The inequality also holds when rho_i=0 since s>0. Summing nonnegative terms and using F002 gives sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1). Since V was an arbitrary delta-cover, taking the infimum gives H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1). Discharge L2 in this universal cover conclusion. Since delta>0 was arbitrary and delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, H^s(I)=infinity. N001 gives dim_H(I)≥s. Let s increase to 1 to get dim_H(I)≥1, and discharge L3. Together with F001 this is dim_H(I)=1 and all the measure assertions of N003.

locals.declaration: Choose a countable r-cover W of E with total q-cost<epsilon/2, as asserted by F001.
For nonempty W_i of positive diameter set U_i=W_i. If W_i={x}, set U_i to the open Euclidean ball centered at that unique x with diameter beta_i (radius beta_i/2). For empty W_i set U_i=empty.
Set K={i∈N:U_i is nonempty}; use K as the index set after discarding empty members.
For i∈K set r_i(i)=diam(U_i), written r_i in formulas.
For i∈K set N_i(i)=ceil(1/r_i(i)), written N_i.

argument.text: Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Push forward the interval covers that give H^a(I)=0 for a>1 in N003; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0 for all a>1. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a for every a>1 and hence dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L1 and record F000.

produces.statement: If n=0, dim_H(F)≤D+1.

argument.text: For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. Such covers exist, for example by the finite-ball-cover assertion in N002. This is the existence statement F001, before choosing W.

produces.statement: There exists a sequence W of subsets of R^n covering E, with diam(W_i)≤r for all i and sum_i diam(W_i)^q<epsilon/2.

argument.text: Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

produces.statement: The family (U_i)_(i∈K) covers E, 0<r_i≤r≤1 for i∈K, r_i=diam(U_i), and sum_(i∈K)r_i^q<epsilon.

argument.text:
For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

produces.statement: H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.

argument.text: For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. N001, with ambient dimension n+1 and positive exponent q+1, gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). Discharge L3 and L2. This proves F004.

produces.statement: If n≥1, dim_H(F)≤D+1.

argument.text: A natural dimension n is either zero or at least one. F000 and F004 thus give dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. By N002 the right hand side is finite, proving the finiteness clause as well.

locals.type: sequence of subsets of Euclidean R^(n+1)
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary sequence V, temporarily a delta-cover of F.

locals.type: sequence of finite nonnegative real numbers
locals.declaration: Set rho_i=diam(V_i); empty members have rho_i=0.
Set A_i(i)={x∈R^n: there exists t∈R with (x,t)∈V_i}, the horizontal coordinate projection.
Set B_i(i)={t∈R: there exists x∈R^n with (x,t)∈V_i}, the vertical coordinate projection.
Set c equal to the finite real value of H^s_delta(E); N002 proves its finiteness for the positive s and delta.

locals.type: sequence of open subsets of R, each empty or an open bounded interval
locals.declaration: If V_i is nonempty set J_i=(inf(B_i)-eta_i/2,sup(B_i)+eta_i/2); if V_i is empty set J_i=empty.
For all natural i define f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t), with extended nonnegative values. Openness of J_i proves the measurability asserted here in S003.

locals.type: measure on the Borel real line
locals.declaration: Set μ=λ|I, Lebesgue measure restricted to I.

argument.text: Fix s>0, delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L1: V covers F and diam(V_i)≤delta for all i. Empty members may be discarded; equivalently retain them with all ensuing projections and intervals empty and costs zero. Define rho,A_i,B_i and c as declared. Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz for the Euclidean metric in D006: each squared coordinate distance is bounded by the sum of the squared horizontal and vertical distances. Hence diam(A_i),diam(B_i)≤rho_i≤delta. In particular a nonempty B_i is a nonempty bounded subset of R. N002 applies to the positive s,delta and gives c<infinity.

produces.statement: V covers F, rho_i≤delta, diam(A_i)≤rho_i, diam(B_i)≤rho_i, and c=H^s_delta(E)<infinity; nonempty B_i are bounded.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary epsilon>0 and set eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0. Define J as declared. For a nonempty B_i, its supremum minus its infimum equals its diameter and is at most rho_i by F001. Thus B_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i. The empty-member convention makes both assertions true for empty V_i as well. The J_i are open measurable sets and enclose the possibly nonmeasurable projections. This construction needs no measurability of V_i,A_i or B_i.

produces.statement: For every i, B_i⊆J_i, J_i is open and measurable, and |J_i∩I|≤|J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i.

argument.text: Define the nonnegative functions f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t). They are measurable because each J_i is open and each coefficient is a fixed finite nonnegative real. Under L2: t∈I, for every x∈E the point (x,t) lies in F, so some V_i contains it. Then x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Thus the family of A_i with t∈J_i is a delta-cover of E, and the defining infimum and diam(A_i)≤rho_i give c≤sum_i rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The point x here is universally bound in this coverage argument, and i is its existential cover index. Discharge L2 into the assertion for every t∈I. Record F003.

produces.statement: Each f_i is nonnegative and Borel measurable; for every u∈I, c≤sum_i f_i(u).

argument.text:
Set μ=λ|I. It is a measure on the Borel real line with μ(R)=λ(I)=1. Apply M006 with α=R, its Borel structure, index type β=N, this measure μ and the functions f of F003. Borel measurability implies μ-almost-everywhere measurability for each summand. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral and the integral of a constant on a set of measure one give
c≤∫_I sum_i f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i ∫_I f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i rho_i^s |J_i∩I|
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i rho_i^s
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.
Here the middle equality is the integral of a measurable indicator times its nonnegative coefficient. The first inequality inside the sum uses F002 and distributivity of nonnegative sums. Finally eta_i rho_i^s=epsilon*2^(-i-1)*rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)≤epsilon*2^(-i-1), whose sum is epsilon. All sums and integrals are nonnegative and may be infinite; c is finite by F001. This is F004.

produces.statement: c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.

argument.text: If sum_i rho_i^(s+1)=infinity, c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1) holds immediately. Otherwise F004 holds for every epsilon>0 with c and V fixed, so letting epsilon decrease to zero gives the same inequality c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1). The cover V was arbitrary under L1. Take the infimum over all its possible delta-covers of F and discharge L1, obtaining H^s_delta(E)≤H^(s+1)_delta(F). Since s>0 and delta>0 were arbitrary, this is precisely N005.

applications.bindings: Set α=R, m=borel(R), μ=λ restricted to I, β=N, and f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t).
hypothesis_checks: D008 gives Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line; restriction to the Borel interval I is a measure on that same measurable space, as defined at S004.
The index type is N, which is countable.
F003, established in S003 from openness of J_i and constant nonnegative coefficients, proves Borel measurability of every f_i, hence almost-everywhere measurability for the restricted measure.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary positive lower bound T.

argument.text: Temporarily assume L1: D>0 and L2: 0<s<D for arbitrary real s. N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. By its definition as the supremum of scale contents, for every T>0 there exists delta>0 with H^s_delta(E)>T. Moreover these contents are nondecreasing as scale decreases, because a cover admissible at a smaller scale is admissible at any larger one. Thus such lower bounds also hold at arbitrarily small scales. N005 applies at each such delta and gives H^(s+1)_delta(F)≥H^s_delta(E)>T. Its supremum is therefore infinite: H^(s+1)(F)=infinity. Since s+1>0, N001 gives dim_H(F)≥s+1. Record F001.

produces.statement: dim_H(F)≥s+1.

argument.text: By N002, D is a finite real number; under L1 it is positive. F001 holds for every s with 0<s<D. Such s can increase to D, so their s+1 have supremum D+1 and dim_H(F)≥D+1. Equivalently any number below D+1 is below some s+1 with 0<s<D. Discharge L2 in this universal limiting argument, and then discharge L1 to obtain the full conditional statement N006.

locals.type: sequence of subsets of Euclidean R^(n+1)
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary sequence V, temporarily a delta-cover of F.

argument.text: Temporarily assume L1: D=0. By H002 choose x_0∈E and define f(t)=(x_0,t). The Euclidean metric formula in D006 gives dist(f(t),f(u))=|t-u| for all real t,u, including n=0. Thus f restricts to an isometric embedding of I into F.

produces.statement: The restriction of f to I is an isometric embedding and f(I)⊆F.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary s under L2: 0<s<1. For any delta>0 and arbitrary V under L3: V is a delta-cover of F, define W as declared. F001 shows W covers I, and isometry gives diam(W_i)≤diam(V_i)≤delta. Hence H^s_delta(I)≤sum_i diam(V_i)^s. Take the infimum over V, discharge L3, and then take the supremum over positive delta to get H^s(I)≤H^s(F). This proves the particular dimension-monotonicity implication used here directly from covers. N003 gives H^s(I)=infinity, so H^s(F)=infinity. N001 applied to F and exponent s yields dim_H(F)≥s.

produces.statement: dim_H(F)≥s.

argument.text: Since F002 holds for every s with 0<s<1, letting s increase to 1 gives dim_H(F)≥1. Discharge L2. Under L1, 1=D+1, so this proves the asserted bound. Discharge L1 to obtain N007. The argument used only the isometric embedding from a point of E, and applies unchanged to the singleton ambient space R^0.

N002 gives finite D≥0. Thus either D>0 or D=0. In the positive case N006 gives dim_H(F)≥D+1; in the zero case N007 gives the identical bound, including n=0. N004 supplies dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. Antisymmetry gives dim_H(F)=D+1. Substituting F=E×[0,1] and D=dim_H(E), with the Euclidean identification of D006, proves the complete target P.

spec.full_target:
# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
spec.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, with R^n×R identified with Euclidean R^(n+1), including n=0.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary positive real exponent s.

argument.text: Fix m, A and s as declared. Apply M001 to the Euclidean metric space R^m, its Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale, the formula's covers are exactly the covers in D002: a countable family can be enumerated by natural numbers, padding with empty sets if finite, and conversely a sequence is countable. All nonempty sets allowed at such a scale are bounded, so their extended diameters equal their ordinary finite Euclidean diameters. Empty members have cost zero in both definitions; since s>0, nonempty singletons also have zero cost. Thus the inner infimum is exactly the supplied scale content. The extra scale infinity in M001 adds nothing to the supremum: its admissible covers include all covers at scale 1, so its infimum is at most the scale-1 content. The finite positive extended scales are precisely the positive real scales. Taking their supremum proves F001: H^s(A)=μH[s](A). No dimensional normalization constant is introduced.

produces.statement: H^s(A)=μH[s](A).

argument.text: Use F001 to transport the four critical-exponent facts. Under L1: 0<s<dim_H(A), M002 with nonnegative exponent a=s gives μH[s](A)=infinity, hence H^s(A)=infinity; discharge L1. Under L2: dim_H(A)<s, M003 gives μH[s](A)=0, hence H^s(A)=0; discharge L2. Under L3: H^s(A)=0, F001 makes μH[s](A)=0≠infinity, and M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L3. Under L4: H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L4. These are the complete conditional assertions F002.

produces.statement: If 0<s<dim_H(A), H^s(A)=infinity; if dim_H(A)<s, H^s(A)=0; if H^s(A)=0, dim_H(A)≤s; if H^s(A)=infinity, dim_H(A)≥s.

argument.text: The dimension in D004 is a supremum in the nonnegative extended reals, so it is nonnegative, including for the empty set. The arbitrary choices of m,A,s and F001-F002 prove every clause of N001.

locals.declaration: Choose b>0 with E⊆[-b,b]^n as supplied by F001.
Let h be an arbitrary mesh size, temporarily 0<h≤1.

argument.text: By H003, E is compact, hence bounded in its Euclidean metric. A bounded subset of R^n is contained in a coordinate box [-b,b]^n for some b>0: each coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance, and increasing a bound if necessary makes it positive. This also holds in R^0. Record F001. H001 specifies the nonnegative ambient dimension; N001 gives D≥0.

produces.statement: There exists a positive real b with E⊆[-b,b]^n.

argument.text: Choose b from F001 and define C as declared. Under L1: n>0, fix arbitrary a and h under L2: a>n and L3: 0<h≤1. Divide each coordinate interval [-b,b] into ceil(2b/h) intervals of side at most h. Their number is at most (2b+1)/h in each coordinate, hence the resulting at most C h^(-n) closed cubes cover E. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h. Therefore their total a-cost is at most C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a=C n^(a/2)h^(a-n). Since a-n>0, this tends to zero as h decreases to zero, and their diameters also tend to zero. In particular, at each fixed target scale arbitrarily small h provides admissible covers with costs tending to zero, so H^a(E)=0. Discharge L3 after using the arbitrary mesh sizes. N001 with A=E, exponent a gives D≤a. Since a>n was arbitrary, D≤n (if D>n, choose a strictly between n and D). Discharge L2 and L1. This proves F002.

produces.statement: If n>0, then D≤n.

argument.text: Under L4: n=0, Euclidean R^0 consists of its single empty-coordinate point. H002 implies E=R^0. A cover by that singleton has diameter and s-cost zero for every positive exponent s. Thus H^s(E)=0 for all s>0, and N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, whence D=0 using D≥0. Discharge L4. By H001 the alternatives n=0 and n>0 exhaust the ambient dimensions. F002 and this branch give 0≤D≤n, so D is finite, with the stated singleton conclusion when n=0.

produces.statement: 0≤D≤n, D is finite, and n=0 implies E=R^0 and D=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary positive s and delta. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at the points of E form an open cover. By H003 there is a finite subcover, and each such ball has diameter at most delta. Its finite number of members and finite diameters give a finite total s-cost. The defining infimum therefore gives H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this proves N002.

locals.declaration: Let N range over the positive integers.
Fix an arbitrary sequence V, temporarily a delta-cover of I.

locals.type: sequence of finite nonnegative real numbers
sequence of open subsets of R, each empty or an open bounded interval
locals.declaration: For nonempty V_i set J_i=(inf(V_i)-epsilon*2^(-i-2),sup(V_i)+epsilon*2^(-i-2)); set J_i=empty for empty V_i.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary a under L1: a>1. For each positive integer N, divide I into N closed intervals of length 1/N. They have total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a), which tends to zero as N tends to infinity, while their maximum diameter tends to zero. Thus at every positive target scale the defining infimum is zero, and H^a(I)=0. N001 applied with ambient dimension 1 gives dim_H(I)≤a; taking a down to 1 gives dim_H(I)≤1. Discharge L1 and record F001, including the universally quantified zero-measure assertion.

produces.statement: dim_H(I)≤1, and for every real u>1, H^u(I)=0.

argument.text: Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L2: V is a delta-cover of I. Define rho as declared; each rho_i≤delta is finite. Fix epsilon>0 and define J as declared. A nonempty V_i is bounded, so its real supremum and infimum exist and sup(V_i)-inf(V_i)=rho_i. Therefore V_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1), also when V_i is empty. The open sets J_i cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure and |I|=1 give 1≤sum_i |J_i|≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon, using sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-1)=1. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the required inequality is immediate; if finite, letting the arbitrary epsilon decrease to zero yields F002: sum_i rho_i≥1. All sets measured here are open intervals or I, so no measurability of V_i is assumed.

produces.statement: sum_i rho_i≥1.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary s under L3: 0<s<1. For each i with rho_i>0, rho_i≤delta and s-1<0 give rho_i^s=rho_i*rho_i^(s-1)≥delta^(s-1)*rho_i. The inequality also holds when rho_i=0 since s>0. Summing nonnegative terms and using F002 gives sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1). Since V was an arbitrary delta-cover, taking the infimum gives H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1). Discharge L2 in this universal cover conclusion. Since delta>0 was arbitrary and delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, H^s(I)=infinity. N001 gives dim_H(I)≥s. Let s increase to 1 to get dim_H(I)≥1, and discharge L3. Together with F001 this is dim_H(I)=1 and all the measure assertions of N003.

locals.declaration: Choose a countable r-cover W of E with total q-cost<epsilon/2, as asserted by F001.
For nonempty W_i of positive diameter set U_i=W_i. If W_i={x}, set U_i to the open Euclidean ball centered at that unique x with diameter beta_i (radius beta_i/2). For empty W_i set U_i=empty.
Set K={i∈N:U_i is nonempty}; use K as the index set after discarding empty members.
For i∈K set r_i(i)=diam(U_i), written r_i in formulas.
For i∈K set N_i(i)=ceil(1/r_i(i)), written N_i.

argument.text: Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Push forward the interval covers that give H^a(I)=0 for a>1 in N003; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0 for all a>1. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a for every a>1 and hence dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L1 and record F000.

produces.statement: If n=0, dim_H(F)≤D+1.

argument.text: For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. Such covers exist, for example by the finite-ball-cover assertion in N002. This is the existence statement F001, before choosing W.

produces.statement: There exists a sequence W of subsets of R^n covering E, with diam(W_i)≤r for all i and sum_i diam(W_i)^q<epsilon/2.

argument.text: Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

produces.statement: The family (U_i)_(i∈K) covers E, 0<r_i≤r≤1 for i∈K, r_i=diam(U_i), and sum_(i∈K)r_i^q<epsilon.

argument.text:
For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

produces.statement: H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.

argument.text: For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. N001, with ambient dimension n+1 and positive exponent q+1, gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). Discharge L3 and L2. This proves F004.

produces.statement: If n≥1, dim_H(F)≤D+1.

argument.text: A natural dimension n is either zero or at least one. F000 and F004 thus give dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. By N002 the right hand side is finite, proving the finiteness clause as well.
